authority.legal_name: Bangkok Chao Phraya river-transit network — regulated by the Marine Department (Ministry of Transport), operated by the Chao Phraya Express Boat and the electric MINE Smart Ferry

mandate.summary: The Chao Phraya river boats are core public transport for Bangkok — regulated by Thailand's Marine Department under the Ministry of Transport and run by the Chao Phraya Express Boat and the electric MINE Smart Ferry — carrying commuters and visitors along the river and feeding the BTS and MRT network.
current_priorities: Daily river commuting along the Chao Phraya
Electrifying the river fleet (MINE Smart Ferry)
Cutting Bangkok's road congestion and air pollution

policy_targets.decarb_note: Thailand targets carbon neutrality by 2050, and Bangkok has already launched the all-electric MINE Smart Ferry on the Chao Phraya — but most of the river network still runs diesel express boats.
policy_targets.relevance: Navier is the zero-emission foiling upgrade to a network Bangkok already runs and is already electrifying with MINE Smart Ferry — faster, low-wake river lines that relieve the city's gridlock while extending the electric direction the river has already taken.

precedent.headline: Public river boats are core Bangkok commuter infrastructure, not a novelty.
precedent.network: The Chao Phraya Express Boat runs scheduled commuter lines along dozens of numbered piers from Wat Rajsingkorn to Pak Kret, feeding the BTS at Sathorn — and the all-electric MINE Smart Ferry already runs the river with battery vessels.
precedent.note: Public ferry service is core transport infrastructure here, not a novelty. Navier adds a fast passenger-only foiling layer on the busy corridors.

interpretation_for_navier: Navier is the zero-emission foiling upgrade to a network Bangkok already runs and is already electrifying with MINE Smart Ferry — faster, low-wake river lines that relieve the city's gridlock while extending the electric direction the river has already taken.

domestic_network.note: Candidate boarding points with APPROXIMATE anchor coordinates [lng, lat] for Grok to snap to real piers/terminals during seal. Coordinates are anchors, not sealed geometry. Core mirrors the authority's live public stops; new/committed/study stops are flagged.

domestic_pairs.rationale: The core Old City line — Sathorn up to Phra Arthit and the Rattanakosin temples.
The main north line to Nonthaburi.
Southern line to the Wat Rajsingkorn / Charoen Nakhon side.
Central line to the Grand Palace pier (Tha Chang).
Cross-river shuttle to the ICONSIAM riverfront.
Southern commuter extension toward Rat Burana.
Cross-river temple line (Wat Pho/Wat Arun side to Wang Lang).

regional_links.note: Domestic-only network on the Chao Phraya within Greater Bangkok. Khlong (canal) and Gulf links are secondary and out of scope for this phase.

routing_hazards.instruction: Every domestic leg must be routed through navigable open water with NO land crossings (interior_land_km == 0). Hand-curated waypoints required wherever a breakwater, barrier, bridge pier, reef, headland, naval/exclusion zone or shallows would otherwise be clipped. Use data-clean/uae_hand_waypoints.json format {from, to, waypoints:[[lng,lat]...]}.

hazards.detail: The river runs a strong current and heavy rice/sand barge tows — follow the marked channel and waypoint clear of barge trains and moorings.
The express-boat piers are extremely busy with frequent stops — strict low-wake, geofenced no-foil zones at every pier.
Numerous bridge piers (Memorial, Rama VIII, Phra Nang Klao) sit in the channel — hand-waypoint clear.
River level swings with tide and the monsoon flood season — routing and pier access must account for high-flow periods.
